newsitem.title: GERMANY: Flooded E.German farmland put at 7,500 hectares.
newsitem.headline: Flooded E.German farmland put at 7,500 hectares.

text.p: Some 7,500 hectares of farmland in the eastern German state of Brandenburg have been devastated by Oder river floods so far, agriculture ministry official Hans-Hermann Bentrup told the Berlin daily Der Tagesspiegel.
Soldiers and aid workers in the flood-hit state are protecting weakened dikes from high water along a critical stretch of the German-Polish border.
Up to 76,165 ha of farmland are at risk if the fertile Oderbruch plateau, a low-lying area measuring 850 square kilometres, is completely flooded.
Bentrup said farmers were incurring one thousand marks of losses per ha from damaged crops but this was a rough calculation as far as grain was concerned.
In sugarbeet, vegetable and grazing areas, the losses per ha could be much higher, for example if evacuated cows were not milked often enough.
No animals had been lost so far as a result of the floods and because there were enough feeds and alternative stabling, there had not been any emergency slaughterings.
The state was putting together financial compensation schemes for farmers.
